title: Universal first order thickening of a scheme over another
statement: Let $h:Z\to X$ be a morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme]. A *universal first order thickening of $Z$ over $X$* is a first order thickening $Z\subset Z'$ over $X$ [def-sbc-first-order-thickening], that is a scheme $Z'$ with a morphism $h':Z'\to X$ and a closed immersion $i_Z:Z\to Z'$ [def-weil-closed-immersion] whose ideal sheaf $\mathcal I\subseteq\mathcal O_{Z'}$ [def-sbc-closed-immersion-ideal-sheaf] has square zero, with $h'\circ i_Z=h$ [def-weil-scheme-over-base], such that the following holds: for every first order thickening $T\subset T'$ over $X$ (closed immersion $i_T:T\to T'$ whose ideal sheaf has square zero, structure morphism $b:T'\to X$, $T$ over $X$ through $b\circ i_T$; $T$ and $T'$ arbitrary schemes, not necessarily affine) and every morphism $a:T\to Z$ with $h\circ a=b\circ i_T$, there is exactly one morphism $a':T'\to Z'$ with $h'\circ a'=b$ and $a'\circ i_T=i_Z\circ a$. *Uniqueness up to unique isomorphism:* if $(Z'_1,i_1:Z\to Z'_1,h'_1:Z'_1\to X)$ and $(Z'_2,i_2,h'_2)$ are two universal first order thickenings of $Z$ over $X$, there is exactly one morphism $\varphi:Z'_1\to Z'_2$ with $h'_2\circ\varphi=h'_1$ and $\varphi\circ i_1=i_2$, and $\varphi$ is an isomorphism of schemes over $X$. (Existence is not part of the definition: in general a universal first order thickening need not exist; it exists when $h$ is formally unramified, Stacks Lemma 04F3, and Stacks Definition 04F4 (1) calls that one *the* universal first order thickening.)

source.place: More on Morphisms, Section 04F2 (section-universal-thickening), opening paragraph; Definition 04F4 (definition-universal-thickening) (1)

proof.text: *The notions are well defined for arbitrary schemes.* A first order thickening over $X$ is defined in [def-sbc-first-order-thickening], items (2) and (4), for an arbitrary scheme $T'$ and an arbitrary closed immersion $i_T:T\to T'$ [def-weil-closed-immersion] whose ideal sheaf $\mathcal I_T=\ker(\mathcal O_{T'}\to i_{T,*}\mathcal O_T)$ [def-sbc-closed-immersion-ideal-sheaf] satisfies $\mathcal I_T^2=0$, together with a morphism $b:T'\to X$, $T$ being over $X$ through $b\circ i_T$; affineness is only required in the separate notion 'of affine schemes', which is not used here. So $Z\subset Z'$ with $h'$ is a first order thickening over $X$ exactly when $i_Z$ is a closed immersion with square-zero ideal sheaf and $h'\circ i_Z=h$, i.e. $i_Z$ is a morphism of schemes over $X$ [def-weil-scheme-over-base] when $Z$ is over $X$ through $h$. In the universal property, $h\circ a=b\circ i_T$ says that $a:T\to Z$ is a morphism over $X$, and the two conditions on $a'$ say that $a':T'\to Z'$ is a morphism over $X$ and that $(a,a')$ commutes with the closed immersions (Stacks: '$(a,a')$ is a morphism of thickenings over $X$'). All are equalities of composites of morphisms of schemes [def-pc-scheme], so the defining condition is a well-formed property of the triple $(Z',i_Z,h')$, quantified over all first order thickenings over $X$ and all $a$; nothing is chosen.

proof.text: *Uniqueness up to unique isomorphism.* Let $(Z'_1,i_1,h'_1)$ and $(Z'_2,i_2,h'_2)$ be universal first order thickenings of $Z$ over $X$. Each $Z\subset Z'_k$ is itself a first order thickening over $X$ [def-sbc-first-order-thickening], with $b=h'_k$, and $a=\mathrm{id}_Z$ satisfies $h\circ\mathrm{id}_Z=h=h'_k\circ i_k$. (i) Apply the universal property of $Z'_2$ to the thickening $Z\subset Z'_1$, $b=h'_1$, $a=\mathrm{id}_Z$: there is exactly one $\varphi:Z'_1\to Z'_2$ with $h'_2\circ\varphi=h'_1$ and $\varphi\circ i_1=i_2\circ\mathrm{id}_Z=i_2$. This is the existence and uniqueness of $\varphi$. (ii) Symmetrically there is $\psi:Z'_2\to Z'_1$ with $h'_1\circ\psi=h'_2$ and $\psi\circ i_2=i_1$. (iii) $\psi\circ\varphi:Z'_1\to Z'_1$ satisfies $h'_1\circ\psi\circ\varphi=h'_2\circ\varphi=h'_1$ and $\psi\circ\varphi\circ i_1=\psi\circ i_2=i_1$; so does $\mathrm{id}_{Z'_1}$. The universal property of $Z'_1$ applied to the thickening $Z\subset Z'_1$ itself ($b=h'_1$, $a=\mathrm{id}_Z$) allows exactly one such morphism, so $\psi\circ\varphi=\mathrm{id}_{Z'_1}$. Likewise $\varphi\circ\psi=\mathrm{id}_{Z'_2}$. Hence $\varphi$ is an isomorphism of schemes, and an isomorphism over $X$ [def-weil-scheme-over-base] since $h'_2\circ\varphi=h'_1$.
